calls.reason: This is hedged ('I can't imagine') and has no deadline. The evidence is mixed: Lovable's own account of Plinq is unverified, and Pirxey's travel-app case needed professional remediation. Neither settles it.
A Cursor forum thread confirms Cursor used Claude and shows some complaints next to praise. Nothing from the period measures how many working coders were deeply frustrated.

The RCR census shows a 30% UK consultant shortfall, and RSNA reports US academic shortages. The closest replacement case, in Denmark, moved the radiologist to other work, and no job displacement was found.
The only evidence is a February 2025 baseline survey in which 88% of Americans would encourage others to code. No data over time shows rising discouragement of children.
This forecast runs to at least 2035. The Epoch MirrorCode benchmark and the TechRadar account do not show a large project succeeding without human architectural input.

CMU's 1995 trip had a computer driving over 98% of the way. By 2024, Waymo still ran only in limited service areas, and Nature Communications describes rare cases as a persistent obstacle. That fits the decades-long last-20% pattern.
